tutorial.title: How to set up and use your polar scope
tutorial.intro: A practical walkthrough for a SkyWatcher polar scope on a Celestron Advanced VX — from one-time setup to using it under a dark sky.

s1.title: What polar alignment does
s1.body: Your mount's RA axis must point at the celestial pole so a single motor can track the sky. The polar scope lets you sight the pole star and place it precisely.
tips: The pole is near — but not exactly at — the pole star.
Good alignment = long, round-star exposures and reliable go-to.

s2.title: One-time: collimate the polar scope to the RA axis
s2.body: Center a distant object on the reticle, rotate the RA axis 180°, and adjust the three grub screws to remove half the drift. Repeat until the object stays put as you rotate.
tips: Do this once in daylight on a far landmark (or on Polaris at night).
Adjust the reticle grub screws, never the mount's alt/az bolts.
Tiny turns — the screws are sensitive.

s3.title: Set up the mount (Advanced VX)
s3.body: Level the tripod, set the latitude scale to your latitude, and aim the mount at TRUE north (or south), not magnetic north.
tips: Use a bubble level; an unlevel tripod throws off the latitude setting.
Correct for magnetic declination between compass north and true north.
Pre-set the latitude bolt near your site latitude before you start.

s4.title: See the reticle at night
s4.body: At night you see stars but not the engraved reticle. Illuminate it dimly: shine a RED light obliquely into the front (objective) end, or use the mount's illuminator if fitted.
tips: Red only — white light ruins your dark adaption.
A red phone screen held near the objective works in a pinch.
Keep it dim; too bright washes out faint Polaris.

s5.title: Place the pole star
s5.body: Rotate the RA axis until the reticle's pole-star marker is at the clock position shown above, then use the mount's ALT and AZ bolts (not RA) to move the star into the marker.
tips: Match the on-screen orientation (inverting/erect) to your scope.
Move with the slow alt/az bolts; leave RA where you set it.
Center the star in the small circle, not on the true-pole cross.

s6.title: Verify and refine
s6.body: Cross-check with the Advanced VX hand controller's All-Star Polar Align, or do a quick drift check on a star near the meridian and tweak the alt/az bolts.
tips: All-Star uses any bright star — handy when Polaris is hidden.
Re-check after the mount settles or if you bump the tripod.

paramDocs.saturation: Overall colour saturation of the final image. Higher is more vivid; too high turns stars garish.
paramDocs.star_desat: Pushes the brightest star cores toward white. Fixes solid colour discs on dense clusters and magenta SHO stars. 0 = off.
paramDocs.lum_opacity: Opacity of the L (luminance) layer in an LRGB composite. 1 = all detail from L; lower is softer and more colour-driven.
paramDocs.ha_screen: Opacity of the red Hα layer screened over the image (only when an Hα channel is present). Higher = stronger red nebulosity.
paramDocs.ha_black_point: Clips the Hα layer's background to black so its red lifts only bright HII knots, not the whole sky.
paramDocs.ha_exclude_stars: Screens Hα onto nebulosity only (stars removed first) so the red doesn't tint stars orange/pink.
paramDocs.chroma_blur: Blurs colour noise in the LRGB composite (pixels); the L layer keeps all detail. Higher smooths colour and flattens mottle.
paramDocs.core_highlight_knee: Where the nebula-CORE highlight roll-off begins on the luminance. Below it nothing changes — for blown nebula cores, not clusters.
paramDocs.core_highlight_ceil: How far below white a blown nebula core is capped (with core_highlight_knee). Lower = a deeper, more structured core.
paramDocs.highlight_knee: Where the star-safe highlight cap begins on the final image — keeps bright star cores from clipping to white.
paramDocs.highlight_ceil: How far below white bright star cores are capped (with highlight_knee). Lower = cores stay more coloured, less burnt.
paramDocs.crop_frac: Fraction trimmed off each edge to drop the ragged dithered stacking-edge bands.
paramDocs.palette: Channel→RGB colour mapping: natural, hargb, hoo, sho, hos, foraxx or mono. The narrowband palettes need OIII/SII data.
paramDocs.color_calibration: Photometric colour calibration (SPCC) for natural star/nebula hues; falls back to a neutral balance when offline.
paramDocs.linked_stretch: Stretches all channels together to preserve the calibrated colour balance (vs per-channel, which re-tints).
paramDocs.background_level: Target sky-background brightness for the auto-stretch. Lower = a darker sky.
paramDocs.stretch_headroom: Caps bright star cores this far below white BEFORE the stretch so they keep colour instead of burning. 0 = off; lower = more protection.
paramDocs.background_degree: Degree of the Siril polynomial used to model and subtract the sky background/gradient.
paramDocs.combined_background_ai: A second gradient-extraction pass on the combined RGB — removes the large-scale gradient / brown sky the per-channel pass leaves.
paramDocs.color_denoise_ai: AI colour denoise on the linear RGB — cuts chroma noise without blurring detail (unlike a blur).
paramDocs.star_reduce: StarNet++ star-reduction opacity in the finish: 1 = full stars, 0.5 = halved, 0 = keep all.
paramDocs.fwhm_sigma: Frame rejection: drop subs whose star sharpness (FWHM) is worse than this many σ from the session. Lower rejects harder.
paramDocs.roundness_floor: Frame rejection: minimum star roundness to keep a sub — drops trailed / wind-shaken frames. Higher keeps only rounder stars.
paramDocs.background_sigma: Frame rejection: drop subs whose background is this many σ above the median (clouds, moonlight, gradients).
paramDocs.star_count_frac: Frame rejection: keep only subs with at least this fraction of the best sub's detected star count.
paramDocs.trail_mask_k: Cross-frame satellite/plane trail masking: a pixel above the per-pixel median + k·σ is replaced. Lower = more aggressive; 0 = off.
paramDocs.denoise_lum: Denoise strength on the linear LUMINANCE master — gentle, to preserve galaxy/nebula detail.
paramDocs.denoise_chroma: Denoise strength on the linear COLOUR channels — usually higher, since thin R/G/B sub-stacks are noisy.
paramDocs.background_ai: GraXpert AI background/gradient extraction on each linear master (instead of Siril's polynomial subsky).
paramDocs.stretch: Overall brightness/contrast stretch of the planet/Moon. Higher lifts the mid-tones.
paramDocs.highlight: Highlight-protection point — higher keeps bright craters and the limb from clipping to white.
paramDocs.sharpen: Wavelet detail boost. 1.0 is default; raise for more crater/band detail, lower if it rings or looks crunchy.
paramDocs.clahe: Local contrast / surface relief. Higher is punchier; too high looks harsh.
paramDocs.headroom: Scales the bright disk down before the stretch so highlights don't burn. 0 or 1 = no scaling; in-between reserves more room.
paramDocs.best_percent: Lucky-imaging frame selection: keep only this % of the sharpest frames before stacking. Lower = stricter.
paramDocs.ap_align: Multi-point (planetary) alignment — corrects local seeing distortion across the disk, not just a global shift.
paramDocs.deconv_fwhm: Deconvolution PSF width (pixels) — set near the blur size to recover detail. 0 = off.
paramDocs.deconv_iters: Deconvolution iterations. More sharpens harder but can ring around bright edges.
paramDocs.deconv_alpha: Deconvolution regularisation — higher suppresses noise/ringing, lower is more aggressive.
paramDocs.per_frame_starnet: Runs StarNet++ on every frame before the comet stack (denser fields). Slower, but cleaner star removal.
paramDocs.look: Render style: natural (faithful, soft), iphone (warmer, punchier, deeper sky) or deepsky (bold, dramatic, high saturation).
paramDocs.brightness: Target sky-background level. Lower = a darker sky; higher lifts the Milky-Way core.
paramDocs.saturation_scale: Scales the chosen look's own saturation. 1 = as designed; below 1 tames neon colour; up to 2 for more.
paramDocs.highlight_ceiling: The Milky-Way core's brightness ceiling. Lower = a dimmer, better-protected core; 0 keeps the look's own.
